ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, fold the square paper $ABCD$ so that $AB$ coincides with $CD$, with the crease being $EF$. As shown in Figure 2, unfold it and then fold it once more, making point C coincide with point E, with the crease being $GH$. The corresponding point of point B is point M, and $EM$ intersects $AB$ at N. What is the ratio of $AE$ to $AN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Let the side length of the square be $2a$ and $DH=b$. Therefore, $CH=2a−b$. Because when the square paper $ABCD$ is folded to make $AB$ coincide with $CD$, the crease is $EF$. As shown in Figure 2, after unfolding and then folding again to make point C coincide with point E, the crease is $GH$, and the corresponding point to point B is point M. Therefore, $EH=CH=2a−b$, $DE=AE=\frac{1}{2}\times2a=a$, $\angle BEH=\angle C=90^\circ$. In $\triangle DEH$, $DE^{2}+DH^{2}=EH^{2}$, i.e., $a^{2}+b^{2}=(2a−b)^{2}$. Solving gives $b=\frac{3}{4}a$. Because $\angle DEH+\angle AEN=90^\circ$ and $\angle AEN+\angle DEH=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle ANE=\angle DEH$. Therefore, $\tan\angle ANE=\tan\angle DEH=\frac{AE}{AN}=\frac{DH}{DE}=\frac{b}{a}=\frac{\frac{3}{4}a}{a}=\boxed{\frac{3}{4}}$.

From Figure 1, read that EF is the middle crease of the square, so E is the midpoint of AD; set the square side as 2a, hence AE=DE=a. In Figure 2, read H on CD and let DH=b, so CH=2a-b. method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图1中，ABCD 是正方形，A、B 在左侧，D、C 在右侧；虚线 EF 是竖直的中线，E 在 AD 上，F 在 BC 上，表示第一次折叠使 AB 与 CD 重合。图2中，纸展开后再次折叠，E 仍在上边 AD 的中点，虚线 EF 仍为中线；G、H 是第二次折痕 GH 与边界的交点，其中 H 在右边 CD 上；折叠后 C 与 E 重合，B 的对应点为 M，直线 EM 与左边 AB 相交于 N。推理：设正方形边长为 2a。由图1第一次折叠使 AB 与 CD 重合，EF 是正方形的中线，所以 E 是 AD 的中点，AE=DE=a。设图2中 DH=b，则 CH=2a-b。第二次折叠使 C 与 E 重合，因此折痕 GH 是 CE 的垂直平分线，H 在折痕上，所以 EH=CH=2a-b。又三角形 DEH 中，DE 与 DH 分别沿正方形的上边和右边，互相垂直，所以 DE^2+DH^2=EH^2，即 a^2+b^2=(2a-b)^2。化简得 a^2=4a^2-4ab，所以 4ab=3a^2，b=3a/4。折叠中 C 映到 E，B 映到 M，所以 BC 映到 EM；同时 CH 映到 EH。因为原来 BC⊥CH，所以折后 EM⊥EH。又 AB⊥AE，因此三角形 AEN 是直角三角形。由 EM⊥EH 以及水平、竖直边的夹角关系，可得 ∠ANE=∠DEH。于是 tan∠ANE=AE/AN，且 tan∠DEH=DH/DE=b/a=3/4，所以 AE/AN=3/4。

method.method_draft: Use an analytic coordinate/reflection route. From the figure, place the square as A=(0,2), B=(0,0), C=(2,0), D=(2,2); then the first fold line EF is the vertical midpoint line, so E=(1,2). The second crease GH is the perpendicular bisector of CE because C folds to E. Compute CE: its midpoint is (3/2,1), its slope is -2, so GH has slope 1/2 and equation y=0.5x+0.25. Reflect B=(0,0) across this line to get M, for example using the point-to-line reflection formula; this gives M=(-0.2,0.4). Then write the equation of EM through E=(1,2) and M=(-0.2,0.4): its slope is 4/3, so y-2=(4/3)(x-1). Intersect this line with AB, which is x=0, to get N=(0,2/3). raw_record.original_question: As shown in Figure 1, fold the square paper $ABCD$ so that $AB$ coincides with $CD$, with the crease being $EF$. As shown in Figure 2, unfold it and then fold it once more, making point C coincide with point E, with the crease being $GH$. The corresponding point of point B is point M, and $EM$ intersects $AB$ at N. What is the ratio of $AE$ to $AN$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} Let the side length of the square be $2a$ and $DH=b$. Therefore, $CH=2a-b$. Because when the square paper $ABCD$ is folded to make $AB$ coincide with $CD$, the crease is $EF$. As shown in Figure 2, after unfolding and then folding again to make point C coincide with point E, the crease is $GH$, and the corresponding point to point B is point M. Therefore, $EH=CH=2a-b$, $DE=AE=\frac{1}{2}\times 2a=a$, $\angle BEH=\angle C=90^\circ$. In $\triangle DEH$, $DE^{2}+DH^{2}=EH^{2}$, i.e., $a^{2}+b^{2}=(2a-b)^{2}$. Solving gives $b=\frac{3}{4}a$. Because $\angle DEH+\angle AEN=90^\circ$ and $\angle AEN+\angle DEH=90^\circ$, therefore $\angle ANE=\angle DEH$. Therefore, $\tan\angle ANE=\tan\angle DEH=\frac{AE}{AN}=\frac{DH}{DE}=\frac{b}{a}=\frac{\frac{3}{4}a}{a}=\boxed{\frac{3}{4}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In Figure 1, ABCD is a square, A and B are on the left side, and D and C are on the right side; the dashed line EF is the vertical midline, E is on AD, and F is on BC, indicating that the first folding makes AB coincide with CD. In Figure 2, after the paper is unfolded and folded again, E is still at the midpoint of the upper side AD, and the dashed line EF is still the midline; G and H are the intersection points of the second crease GH and the boundary, where H is on the right side CD; after folding, C coincides with E, the corresponding point of B is M, and the line EM intersects the left side AB at N. Reasoning: Let the side length of the square be 2a. From the first folding in Figure 1 making AB coincide with CD, EF is the midline of the square, so E is the midpoint of AD, AE=DE=a. Let DH=b in Figure 2, then CH=2a-b. The second folding makes C coincide with E, so the crease GH is the perpendicular bisector of CE, and H is on the crease, so EH=CH=2a-b. Also in triangle DEH, DE and DH lie along the upper side and right side of the square respectively and are perpendicular to each other, so DE^2+DH^2=EH^2, that is, a^2+b^2=(2a-b)^2. Simplifying gives a^2=4a^2-4ab, so 4ab=3a^2, b=3a/4. In the folding, C maps to E, and B maps to M, so BC maps to EM; at the same time CH maps to EH. Because originally BC⊥CH, after folding EM⊥EH. Also AB⊥AE, therefore triangle AEN is a right triangle. From EM⊥EH and the angle relationship of horizontal and vertical sides, it can be obtained that ∠ANE=∠DEH. Thus tan∠ANE=AE/AN, and tan∠DEH=DH/DE=b/a=3/4, so AE/AN=3/4.
